causal_chain: Existing and new applications consume more database workload
Consumed usage is billed monthly in arrears
Usage-based revenue is recognized as the service is delivered
Atlas-related revenue grows at the modelled rate
drivers.counterevidence_rationale: The filing itself discloses macro-driven slowing of existing Atlas applications; the low case is built around that headwind rather than dismissed.

evidence_nodes.conclusion: Atlas revenue is usage-based and billed in arrears, so consumption is the recognized-revenue driver.
Atlas rose to 70% of total revenue from 63% two years earlier, evidencing sustained consumption growth.
The issuer reports slower-than-historical growth of existing Atlas applications.

falsifiers: Atlas revenue growth below 7% in any forecast year
leading_indicators: Quarterly Atlas consumption growth disclosed in later filings
Remaining performance obligations recognised within twelve months
drivers.persistence_rationale: Consumption growth has persisted for three audited years but the issuer discloses macro-driven slowing of existing applications, so persistence is not assumed structural.
drivers.thesis: Atlas revenue is recognized on measured consumption; continued workload migration and new application demand raise consumed workload, while disclosed macro pressure slows the growth of existing applications.
drivers.title: Atlas consumption expansion

causal_chain: Direct sales expands the enterprise customer count
Term licences and support renew and expand
drivers.counterevidence_rationale: The filing discloses customer-count expansion and single-digit category growth; no contrary evidence on the enterprise base was found within the opened filing.

evidence_nodes.conclusion: Direct Sales Customers grew from over 6,400 to over 7,500 in two years.
Customers with at least $100,000 of ARR or annualized MRR rose to 2,396.

falsifiers: Other subscription revenue declining in the base case
drivers.persistence_rationale: Customer counts grew each year, but the disclosed category grew only 3.2% in FY2025 as customers migrated workloads to Atlas, so expansion is modelled as low growth.
drivers.thesis: Growth in Direct Sales Customers and in the at-least-$100,000 ARR cohort supports term-license and support revenue, whose growth is far slower than Atlas.
drivers.title: Enterprise estate and large-cohort expansion

causal_chain: Contracted backlog and deferred revenue are carried into the period
Obligations are satisfied as services are delivered
Previously deferred amounts are recognized as revenue
Services and support revenue is partly supported by that stock
drivers.counterevidence_rationale: No independent evidence on services attach or backlog cancellation was read; the high case could therefore be exceeded or missed without a checked signal.

evidence_nodes.conclusion: 748.0 USD million of remaining performance obligations existed at FY2025 year end, 59% due within twelve months.
18% of FY2025 revenue came from deferred revenue outstanding at the start of the period.

falsifiers: Services revenue contracting while backlog grows
Backlog conversion slower than the disclosed twelve-month share
leading_indicators: Remaining performance obligations at each period end
drivers.persistence_rationale: Backlog is a bounded stock that converts within roughly three years; it supports the near-term path but is not a multi-year growth mechanism.
drivers.thesis: Remaining performance obligations and deferred revenue give bounded visibility into near-term recognized revenue, including services delivered alongside deployments.
drivers.title: Contracted backlog and deferred-revenue conversion

growth_driver_tree.rationale: One root per disclosed revenue category: each root maps only to that category's Base growth parameters, and the weights are analyst allocations rather than identified causal effects.

research_coverage.conclusion: MONGODB, INC. reports as a single operating segment; FY2025 total revenue reconciles exactly to three disclosed revenue categories.
research_coverage.rationale: Base perimeter verified against the audited FY2025 consolidated statements of operations.
research_coverage.revenue_mechanism: Recognized subscription and services revenue under ASC 606 equals the reported consolidated total.

research_coverage.conclusion: FY2023-FY2025 revenue grew from 1,284.0 to 2,006.4 USD million, with Atlas-related revenue rising from 808.3 to 1,405.2.
research_coverage.rationale: Three consecutive audited years and the disclosed category split establish the historical curve; forward levels remain analyst assumptions.
research_coverage.revenue_mechanism: Atlas consumption growth plus a slower-growing term-license and support base drives the consolidated curve.

research_coverage.conclusion: No independent database-market size or growth series was read under the bounded one-source research budget.
research_coverage.rationale: A market forecast without a bound, checked primary source would be an invented input; the gap is disclosed instead.
research_coverage.revenue_mechanism: Market growth would bound Atlas consumption expansion, but no measured market series enters the model.

research_coverage.conclusion: Competitive share and pricing evidence is limited to issuer risk-factor statements; no independent share or price series was checked.
research_coverage.rationale: Issuer-authored risk language cannot calibrate a competitive price or share path.
research_coverage.revenue_mechanism: Competitive pricing would change monetization of consumed workload, which the model does not calibrate.

research_coverage.conclusion: Delivery capacity is procured cloud infrastructure under multi-year commitments; no disclosed capacity ceiling constrains recognized revenue in the horizon.
research_coverage.rationale: The filing describes non-cancelable cloud capacity commitments as a margin matter, not a revenue constraint.
research_coverage.revenue_mechanism: Atlas capacity is elastic third-party cloud capacity, so capacity is a cost input rather than a revenue ceiling.

research_coverage.conclusion: The disclosed platform roadmap (vector search, stream processing, search nodes) expands the addressable workload set but has no published revenue conversion.
research_coverage.rationale: Product capability is mapped only to the growth assumption it informs; no separate revenue line is invented.
research_coverage.revenue_mechanism: New workload capabilities raise eligible consumption, which the Atlas growth assumption is conditioned on.

research_coverage.conclusion: Data-privacy and AI regulation are described qualitatively; no quantified revenue exposure or dated compliance cost was disclosed.
research_coverage.rationale: No quantified exposure was read, so the model cannot carry a policy-driven adjustment.
research_coverage.revenue_mechanism: Regulatory change could alter regional demand or hosting topology, which is not calibrated.

research_coverage.conclusion: Direct Sales Customers exceeded 7,500 (from 6,400 two years earlier) and customers with at least $100,000 of ARR/MRR rose to 2,396; over 53,100 Atlas customers were reported.
research_coverage.rationale: Customer and cohort counts are disclosed stocks; they inform direction and level discipline but do not by themselves produce a revenue path.
research_coverage.revenue_mechanism: Larger enterprise cohorts expand committed subscription revenue, which informs the other-subscription growth assumption.

research_coverage.conclusion: Demand growth is measured only through consumption; the filing discloses slower growth of existing Atlas applications under macro pressure.
research_coverage.rationale: Demand evidence is issuer-disclosed and directional; the magnitude stays an analyst assumption.
research_coverage.revenue_mechanism: Consumption growth of existing and new applications drives usage-based Atlas revenue.

recognition.aggregation_boundary: Published Atlas-related revenue aggregates usage-based DBaaS consumption billed monthly in arrears with sales-assisted annual contracts; the exact split between self-serve and sales-assisted consumption is not disclosed, so no finer recognition algorithm is invented.
recognition.trigger: Consumption of the managed database service during the period (usage-based).

base.rationale: Base case: year-over-year growth of the disclosed MongoDB Atlas-related revenue category, driven by the analyst assumptions above. direct_growth is a transparent fallback because the filing discloses no usage, seat, or ARR denominator that could calibrate a native operating model.

recognition.aggregation_boundary: Other subscription combines term-license revenue recognized at a point in time with post-contract support recognized ratably; the disclosed category is already recognized revenue and the license/PCS split is not published.
recognition.trigger: Delivery and transfer of control of the term licence, with support recognized ratably over the contract term.
